title: File Organisation and Access
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Show understanding of why user-defined types are necessary
Define and use non-composite types; enumerated and pointer data types
Define and use composite data types; set, record and class/object
Choose and design an appropriate user-defined data type for a given problem

Show understanding of the methods of file organisation and select an appropriate method of file organisation and file access for a given problem; serial, sequential (using a key field), random (using a record key)
Show understanding of methods of file access; sequential access for serial and sequential files, and direct access for sequential and random files
Describe the format of binary floating-point real numbers
Understand of the effects of changing the allocation of bits to mantissa and exponent in a floating-point representation
Convert binary floating-point real numbers into denary and vice versa
Show understanding of the consequences of a binary representation only being an approximation to the real number it represents (in certain cases)
Show understanding that binary representations can give rise to rounding errors
